body: @jbrockmendel thanks for the report, will try and reproduce tomorrow.

Also, we do nightly testing of development Numba against the latest Pandas release.  It looks like we should be running the failing test you report:

https://github.com/numba/numba-integration-testing/blob/master/switchboard.py#L287-L303

This gathers all the `test_numba.py` files in the `util`, `groupby.aggregate`, `groupby.transform`, `window` subpackages.  However, these integration tests only run Linux for now, so if this is a Mac-only bug, we wouldn't catch it that way.  (We check Numba's own tests on all platforms of course, but we've found downstream projects will find bugs our test suite doesn't catch from time to time.)

@esc: This is something to keep in mind once we migrate numba-integration-testing over to Github Actions.  We may want to run the integration tests on both Linux and Mac when possible.

> It wouldnt surprise me if the pandas tests you're running do a `--skip-slow`, which would miss this test

No, we don't use `--skip-slow`, instead we do the following to run the parts of the Pandas Test Suite that exercise Numba:

```
    def test(self):
        # Testing pandas has special requirements.
        # See: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/37939

        # Obtain all the paths of the relevant test modules. This uses the
        # subprocess module to execute `conda run`, which then runs a single
        # Python command in the correct environment to import the test module
        # and print it's __file__ attribute.

        paths = []
        for module_subpath in (
            "util",
            "groupby.aggregate",
            "groupby.transform",
            "window",
            ):
            path = execute('conda run -n pandas python -c '
                           '"from pandas.tests.{} import test_numba ; '
                           'print(test_numba.__file__)"'.format(
                               module_subpath), capture=True)
            paths.append(path.decode("utf-8").strip())

        # Run pytest on all the testing modules. This again uses subprocess to
        # execute conda run to run pytest in the correct environment on the
        # correct paths of the test module.
        execute('conda run --no-capture-output -n pandas pytest '
                '{}'.format(" ".join(paths)))
```

@mroeschke any idea if the above threading concerns apply to the rolling numba usage?

The first case can exist in rolling numba usage in pandas.

> your code either has a @njit(parallel=True) function that calls another @njit(parallel=True) function from inside a prange driven loop

One of the parallel's can be changed by the user and one we hardcode `parallel=True`. To be super safe for pandas users, we just not hard code the `parallel=True`. That might be easier then telling using to use a different threading backend.

@jbrockmendel could you rerun the tests with this diff to see it goes away?

```
diff --git a/pandas/core/window/numba_.py b/pandas/core/window/numba_.py
index d00be0ea84..a4de31bdfd 100644
--- a/pandas/core/window/numba_.py
+++ b/pandas/core/window/numba_.py
@@ -239,7 +239,7 @@ def generate_numba_table_func(
 def generate_manual_numpy_nan_agg_with_axis(nan_func):
     numba = import_optional_dependency("numba")

-    @numba.jit(nopython=True, nogil=True, parallel=True)
+    @numba.jit(nopython=True, nogil=True, parallel=False)
     def nan_agg_with_axis(table):
         result = np.empty(table.shape[1])
         for i in numba.prange(table.shape[1]):
```
